messages.text: IFRS 16 ka ek simple example bana do, ek junior ko samjhana hai. 3 saal ki office lease, RM 4,000 monthly, discount rate 5%

Theek hai. Pehle lease liability = 36 monthly payments ki present value at 5%/12 monthly. Yeh approx RM 133,300 banti hai. Right-of-use asset bhi initially isi amount pe recognise hoga (agar koi initial direct costs ya incentives nahi). Kya main month-by-month schedule bhi bana doon?
haan schedule chahiye, pehle 6 months kaafi hain

Month 1: opening 133,300, interest 555, payment 4,000, closing 129,855. Month 2: interest 541, closing 126,396. Month 3: interest 527, closing 122,923. Month 4: interest 512, closing 119,435. Month 5: interest 498, closing 115,933. Month 6: interest 483, closing 112,416. ROU asset straight-line depreciate hoga, ~RM 3,703 per month.
perfect. ye excel mein kaise karun bina macro ke
Columns rakho: Month, Opening, Interest (=Opening*5%/12), Payment, Closing (=Opening+Interest-Payment). Next row ka Opening = previous Closing. Opening ka pehla cell =PV(5%/12,36,-4000) se aa jayega.
acha aur Nida ko samjhaun kyun ROU asset aur liability alag alag move karte hain?

Simple line: liability interest ki wajah se front-loaded tareeqe se ghat-ti hai, asset straight-line depreciate hota hai. Isliye shuru ke saalon mein total expense zyada hota hai. Ek chart bana ke dono lines dikhao, junior ko foran samajh aa jata hai.
chart achha idea hai. waise main har Friday 4 baje Nida ke saath ek review session karti hoon, wahan yehi dikhaungi
Achha format hai. Session mein pehle schedule khud banwao, phir chart, phir ek twist: lease modification ya rent-free period. Har hafte ek concept kaafi hai.
rent free period wala twist bhi bana do

Agar pehle 3 months rent-free hain, to payments 33 hongi aur PV kam: approx RM 120,300. Liability aur ROU asset dono isi pe start honge, aur payments month 4 se shuru. Interest pehle 3 months bhi lagta rahega, is liye liability month 3 tak barhti hai.
oh nice ye to tricky hai. ek aur cheez, pivot table mat suggest karna, mujhe nafrat hai unse lol. SUMIFS theek hai
Noted, sirf SUMIFS aur simple formulas. Summary table: =SUMIFS(Interest, Year, 1) waghera, saal-wise interest aur depreciation dikhane ke liye.
bas yehi chahiye tha. shukriya!
Khushi hui. Best of luck with the session!

messages.text: quick q. for a willingness-to-pay study is Van Westendorp enough or do I need conjoint? it's for my MSc thesis on what parents in SEA will pay for kids' reading apps

Van Westendorp is fine if your question is the acceptable price range for one product. Conjoint is better when you want to know how much each feature is worth, like live tutoring versus a parent dashboard. For a master's thesis, Van Westendorp plus a few purchase-intent questions is usually defensible, as long as you discuss its limits.
ok good. I have 412 responses but most came from Quillstep's own parent mailing list. my supervisor already flagged that as sampling bias

That's a fair flag: existing users have already shown they'll pay something. You could recruit a comparison sample through an online panel, or at least compare your sample's demographics to census figures and report the gap.
a panel is out, we're bootstrapping Quillstep and every dollar goes to the product

Then make it a clearly argued limitation. Compare demographics to public data, run the analysis separately for paying and non-paying sign-ups if you have both, and avoid generalising to all parents in the region.
makes sense. Mateo my cofounder keeps telling me to just drop the MSc and focus on the company 🙄 not happening
A lot of founders hear that. Keeping the thesis tightly scoped is the best answer to it: fewer methods, a clear question, and a realistic writing plan.
speaking of scope.. should I add like 10 parent interviews and go mixed methods? or is that scope creep

Interviews would add depth on why parents value certain features, but they need an ethics amendment, recruitment, transcription and coding. With a draft due soon, it's probably scope creep unless your supervisor thinks the survey alone is too thin.
yeah no. survey only, no interviews. decided
Good. Then put your effort into robustness: check the price-point intersections with and without outliers, and report confidence bands.
can you give me a structure for chapter 3

Try: 3.1 Research design and rationale; 3.2 Instrument (Van Westendorp items, purchase intent, demographics); 3.3 Sampling and recruitment, including the mailing-list bias; 3.4 Data cleaning and exclusions; 3.5 Analysis plan; 3.6 Ethics; 3.7 Limitations. Each section can be 400–800 words.
perfect. honestly I only get thesis work done after 11pm these days, daytime is all Quillstep calls 😅
That's a long day. The structure above should let you write in small blocks, one subsection per night. Good luck!

messages.text: explain vesting cliff like im 5

Imagine you get 48 candies for staying four years, one per month. A cliff means you get nothing for the first 12 months, and then on the one-year anniversary you get 12 candies at once. After that, one candy each month. If you leave before a year, you get zero.
lol ok. and what if a cofounder just bails after 6 months, what happens to their shares?

With vesting and a one-year cliff, someone who leaves at six months keeps no vested shares; the company or the other founders can buy back the unvested ones at a nominal price. Without vesting, they would walk away with their full stake. Many founders use four-year vesting with a one-year cliff for exactly this reason.
makes sense, thx

messages.text: ek corporate gala plan kar rahi hoon, 300 guests, Tempelhof ke hangar mein. run-of-show ka template bana do

Zaroor. Basic run-of-show: 18:00 doors + welcome drink, 18:45 guests seated, 19:00 host welcome, 19:10 CEO speech, 19:25 starter, 20:00 awards block 1, 20:30 main course, 21:15 awards block 2, 21:45 dessert + band, 23:00 last call. Har line ke saath owner aur cue column rakho.
awards 2 blocks mein hi theek hai. AV ke liye kya kya columns chahiye?
AV sheet mein: cue number, time, mic (handheld/lapel), slide/video file, light state, sound cue, aur standby call. Ek 'fallback' column bhi rakho agar video na chale.
fallback wala idea acha hai. caterer bol raha hai 300 ke liye 22 servers chahiye, zyada nahi?
Plated dinner ke liye 1 server per 10-12 guests normal hai, to 25-30 bhi ho sakte hain. Buffet ho to 22 kaafi hain. Kya plated hai?
plated hai. chalo 26 kar deti hoon
Theek hai, 26 servers plus 2 captains rakho. Courses ke beech 12-15 minute ka clearing time run-of-show mein add kar do.
waise ye mera Spreeblick ke saath last event hai, 4 September ko. resignation Monday ko de di thi 🥲
Bohot achha send-off event hai phir! Agar chaho to handover ke liye bhi ek checklist bana sakti hoon taake agla planner aasani se le le.
haan wo baad mein. abhi dietary ka matrix chahiye
Matrix: guest name, table, diet (veg/vegan/halal/kosher/gluten-free), allergies, course-wise substitution, aur kitchen ticket colour. 300 guests mein 10-15% special meals expect karo.
halal ka alag column rakho please, client ke 40 log hain
Ho gaya, halal ka alag column aur count summary upar. Kitchen ko halal plates alag colour ke ticket se bhejo.
shukriya. last cheez, rain plan? hangar hai to indoor hi hai but arrival outside hai
Arrival ke liye covered walkway ya marquee rent karo, aur 100 umbrellas standby. Coat check capacity bhi double rakho agar barish ho.

7/9 ≈ 0.78 so mixed high AG + normal AG acidosis?

Correct: for acute respiratory acidosis HCO3 rises about 1 per 10 rise in CO2, so 26 fits. You're stronger at these than you think.

messages.text: stat mech drill please. GRE style, multiple choice, one at a time

Q1: A system has two energy levels, 0 and ε, each non-degenerate. At temperature T, what is the probability of finding it in the upper level? (A) e^(−ε/kT) (B) 1/(1+e^(ε/kT)) (C) 1/(1+e^(−ε/kT)) (D) ½
B
Correct. Z = 1 + e^(−ε/kT), so P(upper) = e^(−ε/kT)/Z = 1/(1+e^(ε/kT)). Q2: For an ideal monatomic gas, what's the molar heat capacity at constant volume? (A) R/2 (B) R (C) 3R/2 (D) 5R/2
C obviously
Yes, 3R/2 from three translational degrees of freedom. Q3: The Fermi energy of a 3D electron gas scales with number density n as: (A) n^(1/3) (B) n^(2/3) (C) n (D) n^(3/2)
uhh A?
Not quite: it's (B), n^(2/3). k_F scales as n^(1/3) and E_F ∝ k_F², so the exponent doubles. This is a common trap on the test.
argh. ok one more
Q4: Entropy of mixing for two different ideal gases, each one mole, at the same T and P: (A) 0 (B) R ln 2 (C) 2R ln 2 (D) R/2
C
Correct, ΔS = −nR Σ x ln x = 2R ln 2. You're three for four. Your errors are in scaling arguments, so it's worth drilling dimensional reasoning.
honestly if I bomb this should I just retake in April? or is that too late for applications

That depends on each programme's deadline; many close in December or January, so an April score would usually be too late for this cycle. Better to focus on the next few weeks. Want five more scaling questions?
yes, tomorrow. brain's done

messages.text: Explain bootstrapping for my MSc class tomorrow in a way that doesn't need heavy maths. They know the CLT.

Try this: we usually have only one sample, but we want to know how much a statistic like the mean would wobble if we could sample again. Bootstrapping pretends our sample is the population: we resample from it with replacement thousands of times, compute the statistic each time, and look at the spread. That spread approximates the sampling distribution, without needing a formula.

x <- c(12, 15, 9, 20, 14, 11, 17)
boot_means <- replicate(5000, mean(sample(x, replace = TRUE)))

messages.text: ok I need a study plan. I'm sitting the IPC exam (Interior Practice Certification) sometime in August, haven't got the exact date yet. it's three papers: codes & compliance, professional practice, and a design brief under time pressure

That's a good amount of runway: roughly 14 weeks. I'd split it into three phases: foundations (weeks 1-5), practice papers (weeks 6-11) and timed mocks plus review (weeks 12-14). Codes and compliance usually needs the most repetition, so give it a little more weight early. How many hours a week can you realistically give it?
maybe 10? I do 6 to 8 every weekday morning at the State Library before work, that's my best brain time

Ten hours a week works. Two hours each weekday morning gives you exactly that, which leaves weekends free for rest or an occasional mock. I'd keep Fridays lighter, for review rather than new material.
sounds good. what's the best way to memorise the building classes and egress rules? they all blur together

Most people find it easier to anchor rules to real buildings. Pick one example building for each class and annotate a floor plan with the egress distances and fire separation it needs. Spaced repetition flashcards also help for the raw numbers.
honestly flashcards don't work for me at all, I learn by drawing. if I sketch it I remember it

Then lean into that. Make a sketchbook just for the exam: one page per building class with a quick plan, the exits, travel distances and required ratings written onto the drawing. Redraw each page from memory a week later and compare.
love that. ok and the timed design brief - in practice it's 3 hours for a full concept. at work at Halcyon & Reed I'd get two weeks for that lol

The timed brief rewards a fixed routine more than talent. Spend 20 minutes reading and listing constraints, 30 minutes on zoning diagrams, 90 on the main plan and two key views, and keep 40 for notes and checking. Practise that sequence until it's automatic.
ok that's actually helpful. would joining a study group be worth it?

It can be, especially for professional practice questions where discussing scenarios helps. You might look for an IPC study group in Melbourne that meets weekly, or start one with a couple of colleagues.
nah I don't think so, I'm better alone and my evenings are already chaos. can you put the 14 weeks into a table?

Here's the outline: Weeks 1-5 codes and compliance foundations with the sketchbook method, plus one professional practice chapter a week. Weeks 6-11 one past paper section every Friday and weak-topic redraws. Weeks 12-14 two full timed mocks on Saturdays and light review on weekdays. I can expand any week into daily tasks.

A quick test: if you control it fully, it's an output; if it depends on the participant changing, it's an outcome.

ok. how specific do the savings need to be

Give a range with a source. For example: 'Based on AquaNord's design and published trials for similar soils, we expect to reduce irrigation water by 35-45%, around 9,000 cubic metres a season.' If you have last year's water meter readings, include them.

For capacity, you can say the owner manages day-to-day operations with seasonal help.

messages.text: how do i integrate x*e^x again, i always forget which bit is u

Use integration by parts with u = x and dv = e^x dx. Then du = dx and v = e^x, so the integral is x e^x minus the integral of e^x, which gives x e^x - e^x + C. The LIATE rule helps: pick the algebraic term as u before the exponential.
ohh LIATE. ok and x^2 e^x is just doing it twice?
Exactly. First pass with u = x^2 gives x^2 e^x minus 2 times the integral of x e^x, and you already know that one. Final answer: e^x (x^2 - 2x + 2) + C.

messages.text: flutter mein 'setState() called after dispose()' error aa raha hai, jab user screen se jaldi back kar le aur API response baad mein aaye

Ye tab hota hai jab async kaam khatam hone tak widget tree se hat chuka hota hai. Sabse seedha fix: setState se pehle `if (!mounted) return;` check lagayein. Behtar ye hai ke request ko cancel karein dispose() mein, maslan CancelToken ya StreamSubscription.cancel() se.
mounted check laga diya, chal gaya. cancel token Dio mein kaise?

Dio mein `final _cancel = CancelToken();` banayein, request mein `cancelToken: _cancel` pass karein, aur dispose() mein `_cancel.cancel();` call karein. Phir catch mein DioExceptionType.cancel ko ignore kar dein.
perfect bhai

messages.text: ek sawal, agar hum 4 million pre-money valuation maangein to kya zyada hai seed ke liye? GCC mein

Ye traction aur market par depend karta hai. GCC mein early-stage consumer startups ke seed rounds aksar 2 se 5 million dollar pre-money ke darmiyan hote hain. Agar aap ke paas paying subscribers aur achi retention hai to upper side justify ho sakti hai; warna investors kam ki taraf push karenge.
acha aur SAFE vs priced round?

SAFE tez aur sasta hota hai, valuation baad mein set hoti hai, isliye chhote rounds mein common hai. Priced round mein shares aur valuation abhi fix hoti hai aur legal kaam zyada hota hai. Kuch GCC investors priced round pasand karte hain, to pehle lead investor se poochna behtar hai.
theek, shukriya

messages.text: quick refresher: how did IFRS 16 change lease accounting vs IAS 17?

Under IAS 17, lessees split leases into finance leases (on balance sheet) and operating leases (just an expense). IFRS 16 removed that split for lessees: almost all leases now go on the balance sheet as a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. The expense becomes depreciation plus interest, so EBITDA usually goes up. Short-term and low-value leases can still be expensed.
ah yes. and lessors?
Lessor accounting barely changed: they still classify leases as finance or operating, much like IAS 17.

pricing, thinking PKR 4,000 a month per clinic. too much?
